components.note: 口 (mouth) — sound and speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问.
斤 (jīn, axe) is only a loose clue for tīng; the traditional 聽 had 耳 ear.
人 (person) — three persons 人人人: a crowd. Also in 观众 audience, 大众 the public.

example.hanzi: 演讲结束后,听众热烈鼓掌。
example.pinyin: Yǎnjiǎng jiéshù hòu, tīngzhòng rèliè gǔzhǎng.
example.english: After the speech ended, the audience applauded warmly.
example.fact: Orson Welles's 1938 radio adaptation of 'The War of the Worlds' famously led some listeners to briefly believe a real Martian invasion was underway, though historians have since shown that contemporary newspapers considerably exaggerated the scale of the panic.

examples.hanzi: 听众们被这首歌深深吸引了。
examples.pinyin: Tīngzhòngmen bèi zhè shǒu gē shēnshēn xīyǐn le.
examples.english: The audience was deeply drawn in by this song.

examples.hanzi: 这个电台节目有很多忠实听众。
examples.pinyin: Zhège diàntái jiémù yǒu hěn duō zhōngshí tīngzhòng.
examples.english: This radio program has many loyal listeners.

components.note: 山 (mountain) — 山 is a mountain, as in 岛, 岁; 崩 is a mountain collapsing.
朋 (péng) — near sound — 崩 is bēng; 朋 also sounds out 棚 péng and 绷 bēng.

example.hanzi: 山崩了，路被堵住了。
example.pinyin: Shān bēng le, lù bèi dǔzhù le.
example.english: The mountain collapsed and blocked the road.
example.fact: 崩 gives 崩溃 (to break down), 雪崩 (avalanche), 崩塌 (collapse). In modern speech 我崩溃了 means 'I'm losing it'. Historically it was used for the death of an emperor.

examples.hanzi: 雪山崩了，很危险。
examples.pinyin: Xuěshān bēng le, hěn wēixiǎn.
examples.english: The snow mountain collapsed, and it was dangerous.

examples.hanzi: 他一听这个消息，情绪崩溃了。
examples.pinyin: Tā yì tīng zhège xiāoxi, qíngxù bēngkuì le.
examples.english: On hearing the news, his emotions broke down.

components.note: 纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord: 红, 给, 线; here weaving cloth, then organizing.
只 (zhī) matches the sound; the same part is in 职 zhí and 识 shí.

example.hanzi: 奶奶在织毛衣。
example.pinyin: Nǎinai zài zhī máoyī.
example.english: Grandma is knitting a sweater.
example.fact: 织 gives 织布 (weave cloth), 织毛衣 (knit a jumper), and 组织 (organisation, literally weave together). 织女 is the Weaver Girl in the Qixi legend.

examples.hanzi: 她喜欢织围巾送给朋友。
examples.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan zhī wéijīn sòng gěi péngyou.
examples.english: She likes knitting scarves for her friends.

examples.hanzi: 他们在工厂里织布。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zài gōngchǎng lǐ zhī bù.
examples.english: They weave cloth in the factory.

components.note: 攵 (tap, action) — marks hitting or doing, as in 放 release, 改 change, 教 teach; 赦 is releasing someone from punishment.
赤 (chì) — loose sound hint (shè vs chì); 赤 also means bare, as in 赤手 bare-handed.
⺈ (bent figure) — top part, a person; with 口 and 儿 it forms 免. Origin unclear; Memory aid: a person with a hat slipping out, 'excused'.
儿 (legs) — the bottom part and radical, a walking person, as in 先 first and 兄 older brother.

example.hanzi: 总统决定赦免这名囚犯。
example.pinyin: Zǒngtǒng juédìng shèmiǎn zhè míng qiúfàn.
example.english: The president decided to pardon this prisoner.
example.fact: The US Constitution grants the president broad power to pardon federal offenses. One of the most controversial uses of that power was President Gerald Ford's 1974 pardon of Richard Nixon, issued before Nixon had been formally charged with any crime.

examples.hanzi: 国王赦免了那些犯小罪的人。
examples.pinyin: Guówáng shèmiǎn le nàxiē fàn xiǎozuì de rén.
examples.english: The king pardoned those who had committed minor crimes.

examples.hanzi: 他请求政府赦免自己的罪行。
examples.pinyin: Tā qǐngqiú zhèngfǔ shèmiǎn zìjǐ de zuìxíng.
examples.english: He asked the government to pardon his crime.

components.note: 来 (come, wheat) — traditional 麥 combined 來 (the old word for the wheat plant) with a foot 夂 — a grain brought in; 麦 is the wheat radical.
片 (slice) — the right half of 木 split down the middle: a flat piece. See 版 bǎn (printing plate) and 牌 pái (card).

example.hanzi: 早餐我喜欢吃一碗麦片。
example.pinyin: Zǎocān wǒ xǐhuan chī yī wǎn màipiàn.
example.english: I like to eat a bowl of oatmeal for breakfast.
example.fact: Oats are unusually rich in a soluble fiber called beta-glucan, which clinical studies have shown can help lower LDL cholesterol — evidence strong enough that the US FDA has allowed heart-health claims on oat products since 1997.

examples.hanzi: 我每天早上用牛奶泡一碗麦片。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān zǎoshang yòng niúnǎi pào yì wǎn màipiàn.
examples.english: Every morning I soak a bowl of oatmeal in milk.

examples.hanzi: 超市里的麦片种类很多。
examples.pinyin: Chāoshì lǐ de màipiàn zhǒnglèi hěn duō.
examples.english: The supermarket has many kinds of cereal.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, from 肉) — marks body parts, as in 肚, 脸, 腿; 肋 is the ribs.
力 (lì) — close sound: 肋 lèi. 力 means strength, which also suits ribs as the body's frame.
骨 (bone) — 骨 is the bone radical, as in 骼, 髓, 体; 骨 is bones, with ⺼ (flesh) beneath.

example.hanzi: 他摔倒时摔断了两根肋骨。
example.pinyin: Tā shuāidǎo shí shuāiduàn le liǎng gēn lèigǔ.
example.english: He broke two ribs when he fell.
example.fact: Most people are born with 12 pairs of ribs, but roughly 1 in 200 people has an extra rib near the neck, called a cervical rib, which is usually harmless but can occasionally press on nearby nerves or blood vessels.

examples.hanzi: 我咳嗽的时候，肋骨有点疼。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ késou de shíhou, lèigǔ yǒudiǎn téng.
examples.english: My ribs hurt a little when I cough.

examples.hanzi: 这道菜用的是猪肋骨。
examples.pinyin: Zhè dào cài yòng de shì zhū lèigǔ.
examples.english: This dish uses pork ribs.

components.note: 钅 (metal; traditional 金) — marks metals and metal objects, as in 钟 bell/clock, 钱 money; 铃 is a small metal bell.
令 (lìng) — close sound: 铃 líng. 令 also sounds out 零 líng and 龄 líng.
聲 (traditional) — a hanging stone chime struck, with 耳 (ear) below: a sound you hear. 声 keeps only the top, so the picture is mostly lost.
士 (scholar) — the top of 声 is only a leftover of the old chime, not 'scholar'. Do not read meaning into it.

example.hanzi: 手机的铃声突然响了起来。
example.pinyin: Shǒujī de língshēng tūrán xiǎng le qǐlái.
example.english: The phone's ringtone suddenly rang.
example.fact: Nokia's iconic default ringtone, the 'Nokia Tune,' is adapted from a passage of 'Gran Vals,' a nineteenth-century classical guitar piece by Spanish composer Francisco Tárrega, and became one of the most-heard melodies in the world during mobile phones' peak popularity in the 2000s.

examples.hanzi: 下课铃声一响，学生们都跑出了教室。
examples.pinyin: Xiàkè língshēng yì xiǎng, xuéshengmen dōu pǎo chū le jiàoshì.
examples.english: As soon as the bell rang, the students ran out of the classroom.

examples.hanzi: 我把手机铃声调成了静音。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ shǒujī língshēng tiáo chéng le jìngyīn.
examples.english: I set my phone's ringtone to silent.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — body parts, as in 腿 leg, 脸 face.
却 (què) is only a loose sound clue for jiǎo.
止 (foot) — two footprints, one above the other, make a step; the same 止 is in 走 walk and 跑 run.

example.hanzi: 楼梯上传来沉重的脚步声。
example.pinyin: Lóutī shàng chuánlái chénzhòng de jiǎobù shēng.
example.english: Heavy footsteps could be heard on the stairs.
example.fact: Because each person's stride length, foot angle, and weight distribution form a distinctive pattern, forensic gait analysis can sometimes help identify individuals from CCTV footage of nothing more than their footsteps.

examples.hanzi: 我听到门外传来熟悉的脚步声。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ tīngdào mén wài chuánlái shúxī de jiǎobù shēng.
examples.english: I heard familiar footsteps outside the door.

examples.hanzi: 他放慢脚步，等着后面的朋友。
examples.pinyin: Tā fàngmàn jiǎobù, děngzhe hòumiàn de péngyou.
examples.english: He slowed his pace to wait for his friend behind.

components.note: 火 (fire) — fire above a person (儿 legs) — a person carrying fire gives light; 光 is bright and shining, as in 阳光, 时光.
儿 (legs, person) — the bottom 儿 is a walking person, seen also in 先, 兄, 元.
艹 (grass, 草字头) — marks plants and grass, as in 花 flower, 草 grass; 芒 is silvergrass, and by extension a sharp tip or ray, as in 光芒.
亡 (wáng) — only a loose hint (máng vs wáng); same part sounds out 忙 máng and 盲 máng.

example.hanzi: 太阳的光芒照耀着大地。
example.pinyin: Tàiyáng de guāngmáng zhàoyào zhe dàdì.
example.english: The sun's rays shine down on the earth.
example.fact: Sunlight takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to travel the roughly 150 million kilometers from the Sun's surface to Earth, meaning we always see the Sun slightly as it looked a few minutes in the past.

examples.hanzi: 月亮的光芒照在湖面上。
examples.pinyin: Yuèliang de guāngmáng zhào zài húmiàn shàng.
examples.english: The moon's glow shines on the surface of the lake.

examples.hanzi: 这个年轻人的才华闪耀着光芒。
examples.pinyin: Zhège niánqīngrén de cáihuá shǎnyào zhe guāngmáng.
examples.english: This young man's talent shines brightly.

components.note: 隹 (zhuī, short-tailed bird) — 难 was first the name of a bird; "hard" is a borrowed use. The 又 here stands in for the traditional left part.
关 (close) — simplified from 關, a gate 门 with a bolt across it; 关 also means "concern", as in 关系.

example.hanzi: 公司正在努力度过这个难关。
example.pinyin: Gōngsī zhèngzài nǔlì dùguò zhège nánguān.
example.english: The company is working hard to get through this difficult period.
example.fact: After a devastating 1985 earthquake, Mexico City built one of the world's first citywide seismic early-warning systems, using sensors near the Pacific coast that can give residents up to about 60 seconds of warning before shaking from a major quake arrives.

examples.hanzi: 我们一起努力，一定能渡过难关。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yìqǐ nǔlì, yídìng néng dùguò nánguān.
examples.english: If we work together, we can definitely get through this difficulty.

examples.hanzi: 这个难关很不好过，但他没有放弃。
examples.pinyin: Zhège nánguān hěn bù hǎo guò, dàn tā méiyǒu fàngqì.
examples.english: This hurdle was hard to get past, but he didn't give up.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical for actions — 掉 is to drop or lose hold.
页 (head, page) — in traditional 頭 (豆 + 页): 页 is an old picture of a head, as in 顶, 领, 额. 头 dropped both parts.
大 (big) — the bottom. Memory aid: a big 大 body with two dots ⺀ like eyes above — the head, as in 头发. The dictionary's reading is loose.

example.hanzi: 司机在路口掉头。
example.pinyin: Sījī zài lùkǒu diàotóu.
example.english: The driver made a U-turn at the intersection.
example.fact: So-called 'Michigan lefts,' designed in the 1960s, route drivers past their intended left turn to make a U-turn at a median crossover instead of turning directly across oncoming traffic — a design shown in later studies to meaningfully reduce crashes at busy intersections.

examples.hanzi: 前面堵车了，我们掉头吧。
examples.pinyin: Qiánmiàn dǔchē le, wǒmen diàotóu ba.
examples.english: There's a traffic jam ahead, so let's turn around.

examples.hanzi: 他突然掉头就走，什么也没说。
examples.pinyin: Tā tūrán diàotóu jiù zǒu, shénme yě méi shuō.
examples.english: He suddenly turned and left without saying a thing.

components.note: 弓 (bow) — bows and tension: 张 stretch, 引 draw, 弯 bend; 弹 is to shoot or spring, and a bullet.
单 (dān) is a loose clue for dàn/tán; compare 禅 chán and 蝉 chán.
艹 (grass, plants) — 艹 marks plants — medicine was made from herbs, as in 药 and 草.
约 (yuē) — near sound — 药 is yào; 约 also sounds out 钓 diào.

example.hanzi: 士兵们检查了弹药的库存。
example.pinyin: Shìbīngmen jiǎnchále dànyào de kùcún.
example.english: The soldiers checked the ammunition inventory.
example.fact: Gunpowder, invented in China during the 9th century by Daoist alchemists searching for an elixir of immortality, was originally used for fireworks and only later adapted for weapons — one of history's more ironic technological accidents.

examples.hanzi: 这批弹药被运往前线。
examples.pinyin: Zhè pī dànyào bèi yùnwǎng qiánxiàn.
examples.english: This batch of ammunition was shipped to the front.

examples.hanzi: 军队的弹药快用完了。
examples.pinyin: Jūnduì de dànyào kuài yòng wán le.
examples.english: The army's ammunition is almost used up.

components.note: 土 (earth) — marks ground and soil; 坠 is falling down to the ground.
队 (duì) — loose sound hint (zhuì vs duì).
入 (enter) — a pointed shape pushing in; not 人 (person), whose strokes spread outward.

example.hanzi: 那颗小行星最终坠入了地球的大气层。
example.pinyin: Nà kē xiǎoxíngxīng zuìzhōng zhuìrùle Dìqiú de dàqìcéng.
example.english: That asteroid eventually fell into Earth's atmosphere.
example.fact: Roughly 48.5 tons of meteoritic material fall into Earth's atmosphere every day, according to NASA estimates — almost all of it burns up as harmless streaks of light before ever reaching the ground.

examples.hanzi: 飞机失控，坠入了大海。
examples.pinyin: Fēijī shīkòng, zhuìrù le dàhǎi.
examples.english: The plane lost control and plunged into the sea.

examples.hanzi: 她一不小心就坠入了爱河。
examples.pinyin: Tā yì bù xiǎoxīn jiù zhuìrù le àihé.
examples.english: Before she knew it, she had fallen in love.

components.note: 幺 (tiny, faint thread) — doubled under 山 mountain: dim, hidden spots in the mountains, hence quiet and secluded.
黑 (black) — marks darkness, as in 墨 ink, 黯 dim; 默 mò (silent) sounds like 墨 mò, with 犬 dog quietly following.
心 (heart) — feelings and thoughts, as in 想, 思, 急; 感 is to feel or be moved.
咸 (xián) is a loose sound clue for gǎn; 咸 also sounds out 喊 hǎn and 减 jiǎn.

example.hanzi: 他的幽默感让整个办公室都轻松起来。
example.pinyin: Tā de yōumògǎn ràng zhěnggè bàngōngshì dōu qīngsōng qǐlái.
example.english: His sense of humor lightened up the whole office.
example.fact: Laughter triggers the release of endorphins in the brain and can measurably lower levels of the stress hormone cortisol — researchers at Loma Linda University found that even anticipating a funny event produces beneficial changes in mood-related brain chemistry before the laughter even starts.

examples.hanzi: 他很有幽默感，总是逗大家笑。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn yǒu yōumògǎn, zǒngshì dòu dàjiā xiào.
examples.english: He has a great sense of humor and always makes everyone laugh.

examples.hanzi: 我喜欢有幽默感的人。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan yǒu yōumògǎn de rén.
examples.english: I like people with a sense of humor.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 停 is a person stopping.
亭 (tíng) sounds exactly like 停; same part in 婷 tíng.
电 (electric) — simplified from 電: 雨 rain over 申, a lightning bolt (申 originally pictured a flash).

example.hanzi: 台风过后,整座城市停电了三天。
example.pinyin: Táifēng guòhòu, zhěng zuò chéngshì tíngdiànle sān tiān.
example.english: After the typhoon, the whole city lost power for three days.
example.fact: The largest blackout in history struck India in July 2012, cutting power to roughly 620 million people — about 9% of the world's population at the time — after a cascading grid failure across northern and eastern states.

examples.hanzi: 昨晚突然停电，我们点了蜡烛。
examples.pinyin: Zuówǎn tūrán tíngdiàn, wǒmen diǎn le làzhú.
examples.english: The power suddenly went out last night, so we lit candles.

examples.hanzi: 停电了，冰箱里的东西会不会坏掉？
examples.pinyin: Tíngdiàn le, bīngxiāng lǐ de dōngxi huì bu huì huàidiào?
examples.english: The power is out; will the food in the fridge go bad?

meanings: (basketball, soccer etc) to get past an opponent

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement, as in 这, 近, 送: 过 is to pass or cross.
寸 here replaces 咼 (guō) of the traditional 過, so it is not a sound clue; 咼 survives in 锅 guō and 祸 huò.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 他用一个漂亮的过人动作晃过了后卫。
example.pinyin: Tā yòng yī gè piàoliang de guòrén dòngzuò huàngguòle hòuwèi.
example.english: He beat the defender with a beautiful dribbling move.
example.fact: Elite soccer players can react to a sudden change in the ball's direction in under 200 milliseconds, faster than the conscious brain can fully process the decision — much of that split-second footwork is thought to rely on trained reflexive circuits rather than deliberate thought.

examples.hanzi: 这个小伙子聪明过人，一学就会。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiǎohuǒzi cōngmíng guòrén, yì xué jiù huì.
examples.english: This young man is exceptionally smart and learns things right away.

examples.hanzi: 他有过人的记忆力，能背下整本书。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǒu guòrén de jìyìlì, néng bèi xià zhěng běn shū.
examples.english: He has an exceptional memory and can recite a whole book.

components.note: 土 (earth) over 火 (fire): the colour of glowing earth and flame, red; 赤 also means bare, as in 赤脚 barefoot.

example.hanzi: 他赤脚在沙滩上走。
example.pinyin: Tā chìjiǎo zài shātān shang zǒu.
example.english: He walked barefoot on the beach.
example.fact: 赤 means red but is also 'bare': 赤脚 (barefoot), 赤字 (deficit, 'red figures'), 赤道 (the equator). 红 is the everyday red.

examples.hanzi: 他赤着脚在草地上跑。
examples.pinyin: Tā chì zhe jiǎo zài cǎodì shàng pǎo.
examples.english: He ran barefoot on the grass.

examples.hanzi: 赤道附近的天气很热。
examples.pinyin: Chìdào fùjìn de tiānqì hěn rè.
examples.english: The weather near the equator is very hot.

components.note: 木 (tree) — a stroke added at the top of a tree marks its tip: the end. Compare 未 wèi with the longer lower stroke.

example.hanzi: 我们周末去爬山。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zhōumò qù páshān.
example.english: We're going hiking at the weekend.
example.fact: 末 gives 周末 (weekend), 月末 (end of the month), 末日 (doomsday) and 粉末 (powder). It is the tree's tip, the opposite of 本 (root).

examples.hanzi: 这个月末，我们要搬家。
examples.pinyin: Zhège yuèmò, wǒmen yào bānjiā.
examples.english: At the end of this month, we are moving.

examples.hanzi: 他喜欢周末睡懒觉。
examples.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan zhōumò shuì lǎnjiào.
examples.english: He likes to sleep in on weekends.

components.note: 日 (sun) — day and time, as in 晴 clear, 早 early, 明 bright; time was read from the sun.
寸 (cùn) stands in for 寺 sì in the traditional 時; sound clue is loose. 寺 also gives 诗 shī and 持 chí.
一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
日 (sun) — day and time, as in 晴 clear, 早 early, 明 bright; time was read from the sun.
寸 (cùn) stands in for 寺 sì in the traditional 時; sound clue is loose. 寺 also gives 诗 shī and 持 chí.

example.hanzi: 她时不时会想起在巴黎度过的那个夏天。
example.pinyin: Tā shíbùshí huì xiǎngqǐ zài Bālí dùguò de nàge xiàtiān.
example.english: She thinks from time to time about that summer spent in Paris.
example.fact: Autobiographical memories tend to cluster disproportionately around ages 15 to 25, a phenomenon psychologists call the 'reminiscence bump' — one leading explanation is that identity-forming experiences during that window get encoded more richly and are recalled more often throughout life.

examples.hanzi: 他上课时不时看一眼手机。
examples.pinyin: Tā shàngkè shí shíbushí kàn yì yǎn shǒujī.
examples.english: He glances at his phone from time to time during class.

examples.hanzi: 我时不时会去那家小店买点心。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shíbushí huì qù nà jiā xiǎo diàn mǎi diǎnxin.
examples.english: I now and then go to that little shop to buy pastries.

components.note: 火 (fire) — fire and heat: 灯, 烧, 炸, 热; 爆 is to burst in flames.
暴 (bào) sounds exactly like 爆, and means violent.
米 (rice) — a picture of grains of rice divided by a line; as a radical it marks grain foods, as in 粉 powder, 粮 grain, 糖 sugar.
艹 (plants) — marks grasses and flowers, as in 草, 茶, 菜; 花 is a flower.
化 (huà) hints at the sound: 花 huā is close, and 化 also gives 华 huá and 货 huò.

example.hanzi: 电影开始前,他买了一大桶爆米花。
example.pinyin: Diànyǐng kāishǐ qián, tā mǎile yī dà tǒng bàomǐhuā.
example.english: Before the movie started, he bought a large tub of popcorn.
example.fact: Popcorn kernels pop because each one traps a small amount of water inside a hard hull; when heated past about 180°C, the water flashes into steam and the pressure buildup ruptures the hull explosively, turning the starch inside into the familiar fluffy puff.

examples.hanzi: 看电影时我喜欢吃爆米花。
examples.pinyin: Kàn diànyǐng shí wǒ xǐhuan chī bàomǐhuā.
examples.english: I like eating popcorn when watching movies.

examples.hanzi: 这锅爆米花是甜的，不是咸的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè guō bàomǐhuā shì tián de, bú shì xián de.
examples.english: This pot of popcorn is sweet, not salty.

components.note: 艹 (plants) — marks grasses, as in 花, 草, 茶; 莎 is a sedge grass, seen in 莎士比亚 Shakespeare.
沙 (shā) gives the sound: 莎 shā, also in 纱 shā and 鲨 shā.
士 (scholar, soldier) — usually read as an axe or weapon, so a warrior or gentleman (士兵, 博士). Memory aid: 士 has the longer bar on top, 土 (earth) on the bottom.
比 (compare) — two people side by side, one lined up with the other; to compare.
亚 (yà) — Asia; as a part it sounds out 哑 yǎ and 娅 yà.

example.hanzi: 莎士比亚一生创作了三十多部戏剧。
example.pinyin: Shāshìbǐyà yīshēng chuàngzuòle sānshí duō bù xìjù.
example.english: Shakespeare wrote more than thirty plays in his lifetime.
example.fact: No one is certain how William Shakespeare spelled his own name — surviving signatures show variants like 'Shakspere' and 'Shaksper,' since standardized spelling didn't exist in Elizabethan England and even his own family disagreed on it.

examples.hanzi: 莎士比亚是英国最有名的作家之一。
examples.pinyin: Shāshìbǐyà shì Yīngguó zuì yǒumíng de zuòjiā zhī yī.
examples.english: Shakespeare is one of Britain's most famous writers.

examples.hanzi: 我们今天在课上读了莎士比亚的一首诗。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen jīntiān zài kè shàng dú le Shāshìbǐyà de yì shǒu shī.
examples.english: Today in class we read a poem by Shakespeare.

components.note: 用 (use) — early picture is debated: a pail, a fenced enclosure or a hung bell. Memory aid: a door-frame 冂 with a cross-bar — a tool 'put to use' (使用, 不用).
力 (strength) — an old picture of an arm or a plough, a tool of effort. As a radical it marks strength: 办, 助, 动, 努, 男.

example.hanzi: 他用力一推,门终于开了。
example.pinyin: Tā yònglì yī tuī, mén zhōngyú kāile.
example.english: He pushed hard, and the door finally opened.
example.fact: The strongest documented human jaw bite force, measured in laboratory tests on the molars, has reached over 4,300 newtons — more than four times an average human bite, though still far below a saltwater crocodile's roughly 16,000 newtons.

examples.hanzi: 你用力拉一下，门就开了。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yònglì lā yíxià, mén jiù kāi le.
examples.english: Pull hard and the door will open.

examples.hanzi: 他用力地握了握我的手。
examples.pinyin: Tā yònglì de wò le wò wǒ de shǒu.
examples.english: He gripped my hand firmly.

meanings: (before a number) to be less than

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
氵 (water radical, 三点水) — water and liquids: 河, 海, 汤; 满 is filled with water, full.
The right half is a short form of 㒼 (mǎn), the sound part, also in 瞒 mán.

example.hanzi: 员工们对新政策表示不满。
example.pinyin: Yuángōngmen duì xīn zhèngcè biǎoshì bùmǎn.
example.english: The employees expressed dissatisfaction with the new policy.
example.fact: Gallup's long-running State of the Global Workplace survey has repeatedly found that only about one in five employees worldwide report feeling engaged at work, a pattern that has held remarkably steady across most years the survey has run since 2009.

examples.hanzi: 他对这份工作的收入很不满。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì zhè fèn gōngzuò de shōurù hěn bù mǎn.
examples.english: He is very dissatisfied with the pay of this job.

examples.hanzi: 顾客对饭店的服务表示不满。
examples.pinyin: Gùkè duì fàndiàn de fúwù biǎoshì bùmǎn.
examples.english: The customer expressed dissatisfaction with the restaurant's service.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 拿, 提; 揭 is to lift off a cover.
曷 (hé) is a loose hint for jiē; 喝 hē and 渴 kě share it.
雨 (rain) — marks weather and moisture, as in 雪, 雷, 雾; 露 is dew.
路 (lù) gives the sound exactly: 露 lù (dew) or lòu (reveal).

example.hanzi: 记者揭露了这家公司的财务造假。
example.pinyin: Jìzhě jiēlùle zhè jiā gōngsī de cáiwù zàojiǎ.
example.english: The journalist exposed the company's financial fraud.
example.fact: The Watergate scandal that led to President Nixon's 1974 resignation was uncovered largely through the reporting of two Washington Post journalists, Bob Woodward and Carl Bernstein, whose key source inside the FBI was kept anonymous as 'Deep Throat' for over 30 years until his identity was revealed in 2005.

examples.hanzi: 这篇报道揭露了工厂的污染问题。
examples.pinyin: Zhè piān bàodào jiēlù le gōngchǎng de wūrǎn wèntí.
examples.english: This report exposed the factory's pollution problem.

examples.hanzi: 他勇敢地揭露了事情的真相。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǒnggǎn de jiēlù le shìqing de zhēnxiàng.
examples.english: He bravely revealed the truth of the matter.

components.note: 穴 (cave, hole) — the radical of holes and hollow spaces, as in 空 empty, 窗 window, 穿 pierce.
犬 (dog) — a dog bursting out of its den 穴: the picture of something sudden and unexpected.
凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.

example.hanzi: 这座山峰在云层中显得格外突出。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò shānfēng zài yúncéng zhōng xiǎnde géwài tūchū.
example.english: This mountain peak stands out remarkably above the clouds.
example.fact: Mount Everest's summit is the highest point above sea level, but measured from base to peak, Mauna Kea in Hawaii is taller overall — over 10,000 meters when the portion submerged below the Pacific Ocean floor is included.

examples.hanzi: 她的成绩在班里非常突出。
examples.pinyin: Tā de chéngjì zài bān lǐ fēicháng tūchū.
examples.english: Her grades stand out in the class.

examples.hanzi: 这篇文章的重点不够突出。
examples.pinyin: Zhè piān wénzhāng de zhòngdiǎn bú gòu tūchū.
examples.english: The main point of this article is not prominent enough.

components.note: 辛 (xīn, bitter/pungent) — 辛 itself means hot and pungent, so 辣 is spicy hot, as in 辛辣; 辛 also appears in 辩 and 辟.
束 (shù) — only a loose sound hint (là vs shù); same part in 刺 cì.
木 (tree) — marks trees and plants, as in 树, 林, 桃; 椒 is the pepper plant.
叔 (shū) — loose sound hint (jiāo vs shū); 椒 appears in 辣椒 chili and 胡椒 black pepper.

example.hanzi: 她做的川菜放了很多辣椒。
example.pinyin: Tā zuò de Chuāncài fàngle hěnduō làjiāo.
example.english: The Sichuan dish she made had a lot of chili peppers in it.
example.fact: The compound capsaicin, responsible for chili peppers' heat, doesn't actually burn tissue — it binds to the same heat-sensing receptors that detect genuinely hot temperatures, tricking the nervous system into registering pain and warmth that isn't really there.

examples.hanzi: 我不吃辣椒，太辣了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù chī làjiāo, tài là le.
examples.english: I don't eat chili; it's too spicy.

examples.hanzi: 院子里种了几棵红辣椒。
examples.pinyin: Yuànzi lǐ zhòng le jǐ kē hóng làjiāo.
examples.english: A few red chili plants are grown in the yard.

components.note: 米 (rice, grain) — 米 is rice and grain, as in 粥, 糖, 精; 粉 is flour ground from grain, then powder.
分 (fēn) — same sound, different tone — 粉 is fěn; 分 also sounds out 份 fèn.
⺈ (bent person) — a person's figure, the top part of 色. Old story: a person (⺈) sitting on 巴 shows how feelings colour the face, hence 'colour, look'; treat as a memory aid.
巴 (bā) — the lower part; dictionary reads the pair as 'what a person desires'. Memory aid: a face reddening with feeling is a 'colour'.

example.hanzi: 她最喜欢的颜色是粉色。
example.pinyin: Tā zuì xǐhuan de yánsè shì fěnsè.
example.english: Her favorite color is pink.
example.fact: The idea that pink is inherently a girl's color is a fairly recent Western convention — as late as the early 20th century, American parenting guides sometimes recommended pink for boys as the stronger, more dramatic color and blue for girls as delicate and dainty, before the association flipped by the mid-1900s.

examples.hanzi: 我给女儿买了一件粉色的外套。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gěi nǚ'ér mǎi le yí jiàn fěnsè de wàitào.
examples.english: I bought my daughter a pink jacket.

examples.hanzi: 天边的晚霞是粉色的，特别漂亮。
examples.pinyin: Tiānbiān de wǎnxiá shì fěnsè de, tèbié piàoliang.
examples.english: The sunset clouds on the horizon are pink and especially beautiful.

components.note: 斤 (axe) — chopping, as in 所, 斩: freshly cut wood is new (薪 xīn is firewood).
亲 (qīn) is a close sound clue for xīn.
土 (earth) — a green shoot pushing up from the ground: growth, birth, life. 生 also sounds out 性 xìng, 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.

example.hanzi: 医院里传来了一个新生儿的哭声。
example.pinyin: Yīyuàn lǐ chuánláile yī gè xīnshēng'ér de kūshēng.
example.english: The cry of a newborn baby echoed through the hospital.
example.fact: A human newborn's brain is only about 25% of its eventual adult size at birth, compared to roughly 90% for a newborn chimpanzee — this extended period of external brain growth is one reason human infancy is so much longer and more dependent than in other primates.

examples.hanzi: 今年的新生有两千多人。
examples.pinyin: Jīnnián de xīnshēng yǒu liǎng qiān duō rén.
examples.english: There are over two thousand new students this year.

examples.hanzi: 新生入学要先交材料。
examples.pinyin: Xīnshēng rùxué yào xiān jiāo cáiliào.
examples.english: New students must submit documents before enrolling.

components.note: 辛 (bitter) — 辛 pictures a sharp tool once used to mark offenders; it means bitter and laborious, as in 辛苦, and is part of 辣 and 辞.
日 (sun) — sunlight falling on everything: universal, common. 普 also sounds out 谱 pǔ.
木 (tree) — three trees make a dense forest; 林 is two trees, 森 sēn adds more.

example.hanzi: 他姓辛普森,是我们公司的新经理。
example.pinyin: Tā xìng Xīnpǔsēn, shì wǒmen gōngsī de xīn jīnglǐ.
example.english: His surname is Simpson; he's our company's new manager.
example.fact: The animated sitcom The Simpsons has run for over 35 seasons since 1989, making it the longest-running scripted primetime series in American television history, surpassing even long-running dramas and sketch shows by a wide margin.

examples.hanzi: 辛普森先生今天不在办公室。
examples.pinyin: Xīnpǔsēn xiānsheng jīntiān bú zài bàngōngshì.
examples.english: Mr. Simpson isn't in the office today.

examples.hanzi: 我的朋友辛普森住在加拿大。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de péngyou Xīnpǔsēn zhù zài Jiānádà.
examples.english: My friend Simpson lives in Canada.

components.note: 皿 (dish) — 皿 is a dish, as in 盘, 盖, 盒; 盛 is to fill a dish, then abundant.
成 (chéng) — near sound — 盛 is shèng; 成 also sounds out 城 chéng and 诚 chéng.
大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.

example.hanzi: 奥运会开幕式是一场盛大的表演。
example.pinyin: Àoyùnhuì kāimùshì shì yī chǎng shèngdà de biǎoyǎn.
example.english: The Olympic opening ceremony was a grand performance.
example.fact: The 2008 Beijing Olympics opening ceremony reportedly cost around $100 million to produce and involved more than 15,000 performers, choreographed in part using massive LED floor panels that were, at the time, among the largest ever built for a live event.

examples.hanzi: 学校为毕业生举办了盛大的晚会。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào wèi bìyèshēng jǔbàn le shèngdà de wǎnhuì.
examples.english: The school held a grand party for the graduates.

examples.hanzi: 这座城市每年都有盛大的灯会。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngshì měi nián dōu yǒu shèngdà de dēnghuì.
examples.english: This city holds a grand lantern festival every year.

components.note: 氵 (water, 三点水) — marks water and liquids, as in 海 sea, 河 river, 汤 soup; 涨 is rising water or prices, as in 涨价.
张 (zhāng) — same sound: 涨 zhǎng/zhàng. 张 also sounds out 胀 zhàng.

example.hanzi: 最近菜价涨了很多。
example.pinyin: Zuìjìn càijià zhǎng le hěn duō.
example.english: Vegetable prices have gone up a lot lately.
example.fact: 涨 gives 涨价 (price increase) and 上涨 (rise). Read zhàng it means 'swell', as in 涨红了脸 ('face flushed').

examples.hanzi: 这个月的房租涨了一百块。
examples.pinyin: Zhège yuè de fángzū zhǎng le yìbǎi kuài.
examples.english: This month's rent went up by one hundred yuan.

examples.hanzi: 下雨以后，河水涨得很快。
examples.pinyin: Xià yǔ yǐhòu, héshuǐ zhǎng de hěn kuài.
examples.english: After the rain, the river rose quickly.

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 场 field, 城 city, 坐 sit.
也 (yě) is a loose sound clue for dì; 也 also sounds out 他 tā and 池 chí.

example.hanzi: 春天来了,大地重新披上了绿装。
example.pinyin: Chūntiān láile, dàdì chóngxīn pīshàngle lǜzhuāng.
example.english: Spring has arrived, and the earth is dressed in green again.
example.fact: Roughly 71% of Earth's surface is covered by ocean, meaning the solid ground usually pictured when thinking of 'the earth' is really the minority terrain of the planet.

examples.hanzi: 这片大地上有无数的故事。
examples.pinyin: Zhè piàn dàdì shàng yǒu wúshù de gùshi.
examples.english: Countless stories happen on this land.

examples.hanzi: 大雨过后，大地变得湿漉漉的。
examples.pinyin: Dàyǔ guòhòu, dàdì biàn de shīlùlù de.
examples.english: After the heavy rain, the ground turned damp.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement, as in 过, 远, 送: coming closer.
斤 (jīn) is a close sound clue for jìn.
来 (come) — it began as a picture of a wheat plant; the sound was borrowed for "come". 麦 (wheat) still shows it, with a root 夂 added.

example.hanzi: 近来天气变化很大。
example.pinyin: Jìnlái tiānqì biànhuà hěn dà.
example.english: The weather has changed a lot recently.
example.fact: 2023 and 2024 were both confirmed by NASA and NOAA as the warmest years in the modern instrumental temperature record, each surpassing the previous record within just a year of each other.

examples.hanzi: 近来我睡得不太好。
examples.pinyin: Jìnlái wǒ shuì de bú tài hǎo.
examples.english: Lately I haven't been sleeping well.

examples.hanzi: 你近来工作忙不忙？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ jìnlái gōngzuò máng bu máng?
examples.english: Have you been busy with work lately?

components.note: 多 (many) — two 夕 stacked, repeated again and again: so "many, much, more".
年 (year) — first drawn as a person carrying harvested grain: one harvest per year. Seen in 今年, 去年, 年轻.

example.hanzi: 他们多年来一直保持联系。
example.pinyin: Tāmen duōnián lái yīzhí bǎochí liánxì.
example.english: They've stayed in touch for many years.
example.fact: The University of Queensland's Pitch Drop Experiment, begun in 1927, is the world's longest continuously running laboratory experiment — the tar-like pitch inside is so viscous that only nine drops have fallen in nearly a century, and no one has ever witnessed a drop actually fall in real time.

examples.hanzi: 这位老师教了多年的书，经验很丰富。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi lǎoshī jiāo le duō nián de shū, jīngyàn hěn fēngfù.
examples.english: This teacher has taught for many years and has rich experience.

examples.hanzi: 多年不见，你一点儿也没变。
examples.pinyin: Duō nián bú jiàn, nǐ yìdiǎnr yě méi biàn.
examples.english: We haven't met in many years, and you haven't changed a bit.

meanings: to be familiar with the situation

components.note: 口 (mouth) — knowing is something you can say aloud; 口 sits in many speech words (问 ask, 告 tell).
矢 (shǐ, arrow) is only a loose sound clue today; the same 知 sound is in 智 zhì (wisdom).
忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 快 happy, 怕 afraid, 忙 busy.
青 (qīng) is a close sound clue for qíng; the series 清 qīng, 请 qǐng, 晴 qíng, 精 jīng.

example.hanzi: 只有少数高层知情这项计划。
example.pinyin: Zhǐyǒu shǎoshù gāocéng zhīqíng zhè xiàng jìhuà.
example.english: Only a few senior executives knew the details of this plan.
example.fact: During the Manhattan Project, information was so tightly compartmentalized that most of the roughly 130,000 people who worked on it, including many scientists, had no idea they were helping build an atomic bomb until it was used in 1945.

examples.hanzi: 对这件事，他一点也不知情。
examples.pinyin: Duì zhè jiàn shì, tā yìdiǎn yě bù zhīqíng.
examples.english: He knew nothing about this matter.

examples.hanzi: 知情的人都不愿意说出真相。
examples.pinyin: Zhīqíng de rén dōu bú yuànyì shuōchū zhēnxiàng.
examples.english: The people who know the inside story are unwilling to tell the truth.

components.note: 来 (come) — it began as a picture of a wheat plant; the sound was borrowed for "come". 麦 (wheat) still shows it, with a root 夂 added.
回 (return) — a swirl or whirlpool drawn as nested squares: it turns around and comes back.

example.hanzi: 他每天来回于家和公司之间。
example.pinyin: Tā měitiān láihuí yú jiā hé gōngsī zhījiān.
example.english: He commutes back and forth between home and the office every day.
example.fact: The average American commuter spends roughly 27 minutes traveling to work one way, adding up to about 224 hours — nearly nine full days — spent commuting over the course of a year, according to U.S. Census Bureau data.

examples.hanzi: 我们来回走了两趟才找到那家店。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen láihuí zǒu le liǎng tàng cái zhǎodào nà jiā diàn.
examples.english: We walked back and forth twice before finding that shop.

examples.hanzi: 从机场到市区，来回要两个小时。
examples.pinyin: Cóng jīchǎng dào shìqū, láihuí yào liǎng gè xiǎoshí.
examples.english: From the airport to the city and back takes two hours.

components.note: 囗 (enclosure) — here a mat; oldest form shows a person 大 lying on a mat, "to rely on", later "cause". 因 also sounds out 姻 yīn and 烟 yān.
木 (tree) — trees and wood, as in 树 tree, 林 woods, 桌 table; the fruit hangs on the tree.
田 (field) here is the round fruit drawn on the tree. 果 also gives the sound for 课 kè and 颗 kē.

example.hanzi: 科学家试图找出这两种现象之间的因果关系。
example.pinyin: Kēxuéjiā shìtú zhǎochū zhè liǎng zhǒng xiànxiàng zhījiān de yīnguǒ guānxì.
example.english: Scientists tried to determine the causal relationship between the two phenomena.
example.fact: One of statistics' most famous cautionary examples is the strong correlation between per-capita cheese consumption and deaths from becoming tangled in bedsheets in the U.S. — a textbook reminder that correlation alone never proves a causal relationship.

examples.hanzi: 任何事情都有它的因果。
examples.pinyin: Rènhé shìqing dōu yǒu tā de yīnguǒ.
examples.english: Everything has its cause and effect.

examples.hanzi: 他相信因果报应，所以总是帮助别人。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiāngxìn yīnguǒ bàoyìng, suǒyǐ zǒngshì bāngzhù biérén.
examples.english: He believes in karma, so he always helps others.

meanings: to take out and show to others

components.note: 凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.
示 (show) — an altar, a table for offerings; as the radical 礻 it marks rites and spirits: 神, 礼, 福, 社, 祝.

example.hanzi: 请出示您的身份证件。
example.pinyin: Qǐng chūshì nín de shēnfèn zhèngjiàn.
example.english: Please show your identification.
example.fact: The modern passport photo requirement is a relatively recent convention — passports didn't commonly require photographs until World War I, when governments tightened border security and needed a fast way to visually verify identity.

examples.hanzi: 上飞机前，请出示登机牌。
examples.pinyin: Shàng fēijī qián, qǐng chūshì dēngjīpái.
examples.english: Please show your boarding pass before getting on the plane.

examples.hanzi: 警察要求司机出示驾驶证。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá yāoqiú sījī chūshì jiàshǐzhèng.
examples.english: The police asked the driver to show his driver's license.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 请, 谢, 话.
兑 (duì) is a loose sound clue for shuō; 兑 also sounds out 脱 tuō, 税 shuì and 悦 yuè.
口 (mouth) — mouth radical for speaking and sounds, as in 吃, 叫, 吗; 唱 is to sing.
昌 (chāng) — same sound, different tone — 唱 is chàng; 昌 also sounds out 倡 chàng.

example.hanzi: 这位歌手擅长说唱和作曲。
example.pinyin: Zhè wèi gēshǒu shàncháng shuōchàng hé zuòqǔ.
example.english: This singer is skilled at rapping and composing.
example.fact: Hip-hop is generally traced to a specific date and place — August 11, 1973, at a back-to-school party in the Bronx, New York, where DJ Kool Herc extended the instrumental breaks of funk records, a technique that became the rhythmic foundation for rapping.

examples.hanzi: 街上有几个年轻人在表演说唱。
examples.pinyin: Jiē shàng yǒu jǐ gè niánqīngrén zài biǎoyǎn shuōchàng.
examples.english: A few young people are performing rap on the street.

examples.hanzi: 他最爱听的是说唱音乐。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuì ài tīng de shì shuōchàng yīnyuè.
examples.english: What he likes listening to most is rap music.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and cloth, as in 红 red, 给 give, 级 level; 经 first meant a warp thread, then "classics, pass through".
巠 (jīng), here simplified to look like 圣, gives the same sound; also in 茎 jīng, 径 jìng and 轻 qīng.
又 (hand) — two hands pass a vessel: one gives, one receives; 授 shòu adds 扌 for "give".

example.hanzi: 这座桥经受住了强烈地震的考验。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò qiáo jīngshòu zhùle qiángliè dìzhèn de kǎoyàn.
example.english: This bridge withstood the test of a powerful earthquake.
example.fact: Modern base-isolated buildings, like Japan's Tokyo Skytree, are designed to withstand major earthquakes by sitting on flexible bearings or dampers that let the structure sway independently of violent ground motion, dramatically reducing the forces transmitted into the building itself.

examples.hanzi: 这个家庭经受了很多困难。
examples.pinyin: Zhège jiātíng jīngshòu le hěn duō kùnnan.
examples.english: This family has gone through many hardships.

examples.hanzi: 这棵老树经受住了狂风的考验。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kē lǎo shù jīngshòu zhù le kuángfēng de kǎoyàn.
examples.english: This old tree withstood the test of the strong wind.

components.note: 辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving, as in 过, 进, 送; 迷 is losing one's way.
米 (mǐ) — near sound — 迷 is mí, the same syllable with a different tone.
亻 (person) — marks people, as in 他 he, 们 plural, 住 live; 你 is "you".
尔 (ěr) is a loose sound clue for nǐ; 尔 also supplies 您 nín (polite you, with 心 added).

example.hanzi: 她买了一辆迷你电动车。
example.pinyin: Tā mǎile yī liàng mínǐ diàndòngchē.
example.english: She bought a miniature electric car.
example.fact: The Mini Cooper, launched in 1959, was designed by Alec Issigonis largely in response to a 1956 fuel shortage — its transverse-mounted engine layout, unusual at the time, maximized interior space while keeping the car's footprint remarkably small, a layout most small cars still use today.

examples.hanzi: 这个迷你风扇可以放进包里。
examples.pinyin: Zhège mínǐ fēngshàn kěyǐ fàng jìn bāo lǐ.
examples.english: This mini fan can fit into a bag.

examples.hanzi: 他有一只迷你小猪做宠物。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǒu yì zhī mínǐ xiǎo zhū zuò chǒngwù.
examples.english: He keeps a miniature pig as a pet.

components.note: 里 (village, land) — in 野 it means land: open country beyond the village, wild, as in 野兽.
予 (yǔ) hints at the sound: 野 yě is close to 预 yù and 序 xù.
食 (food) — eating and meals: 饭, 饿, 饱 (as 饣); 餐 is a meal.

example.hanzi: 周末我们一家人去公园野餐。
example.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen yī jiā rén qù gōngyuán yěcān.
example.english: On the weekend, our family went to the park for a picnic.
example.fact: The modern picnic as an outdoor social meal became fashionable in France and Britain only after the French Revolution, when royal hunting grounds and parks that had been off-limits to commoners were opened to the public for the first time.

examples.hanzi: 天气好的时候，我们喜欢去野餐。
examples.pinyin: Tiānqì hǎo de shíhou, wǒmen xǐhuan qù yěcān.
examples.english: When the weather is nice, we like to go on picnics.

examples.hanzi: 别忘了带野餐垫和水果。
examples.pinyin: Bié wàng le dài yěcāndiàn hé shuǐguǒ.
examples.english: Don't forget to bring the picnic mat and fruit.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — marks crops and grain, as in 种, 季; 秋 is the harvest season.
火 (fire) — grain plus fire: autumn, the season when crops ripen to harvest; 火 is also the only other part to remember.
大 (big person) — a person with a line above the head, marking the sky above; tiān = heaven, sky, day.

example.hanzi: 秋天的树叶渐渐变成了金黄色。
example.pinyin: Qiūtiān de shùyè jiànjiàn biànchéngle jīnhuángsè.
example.english: The autumn leaves gradually turned golden.
example.fact: Leaves turn color in autumn because trees stop producing chlorophyll, the green pigment that dominates through summer, unmasking yellow and orange carotenoid pigments that were present in the leaf all along but simply hidden.

examples.hanzi: 秋天是一年中最舒服的季节。
examples.pinyin: Qiūtiān shì yì nián zhōng zuì shūfu de jìjié.
examples.english: Autumn is the most comfortable season of the year.

examples.hanzi: 去年秋天，我们去北京看了红叶。
examples.pinyin: Qùnián qiūtiān, wǒmen qù Běijīng kàn le hóngyè.
examples.english: Last autumn we went to Beijing to see the red leaves.

components.note: 力 (strength) — effort, as in 助, 男, 努: handling things takes effort. The two dots stand in for 辡 of the traditional 辦.
至 (arrive) — 到 is to arrive.
刂 is the knife form 刀 (dāo), a close sound clue for dào; 到 itself sounds out 倒 dǎo/dào.

example.hanzi: 这件事很难,但他最终办到了。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì hěn nán, dàn tā zuìzhōng bàndàole.
example.english: This was difficult, but he finally accomplished it.
example.fact: When Apollo 11 landed on the Moon in 1969, the onboard guidance computer had less processing power than a modern digital wristwatch, yet it still successfully guided the lunar module to a safe touchdown.

examples.hanzi: 你答应的事一定要办到。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ dāying de shì yídìng yào bàndào.
examples.english: You must follow through on what you promised.

examples.hanzi: 这么重的箱子，你一个人真的能办到吗？
examples.pinyin: Zhème zhòng de xiāngzi, nǐ yí gè rén zhēn de néng bàndào ma?
examples.english: Can you really manage such a heavy box by yourself?

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 推; 探 is to reach out and feel, then to explore.
The right half is a sound part shared with 深 shēn: a loose clue for tàn.
戈 (dagger-axe) — a picture of an ancient weapon on a long pole. Marks weapons and fighting, as in 战 battle, 武 martial, 我.

example.hanzi: 他们在舞会上跳了一支探戈。
example.pinyin: Tāmen zài wǔhuì shàng tiàole yī zhī tàngē.
example.english: They danced a tango at the ball.
example.fact: The tango originated in the working-class port neighborhoods of Buenos Aires and Montevideo in the late 19th century, blending African, European, and South American musical influences — in 2009, UNESCO added it to the Intangible Cultural Heritage list.

examples.hanzi: 他们在街头跳起了探戈。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zài jiētóu tiào qǐ le tàngē.
examples.english: They started dancing the tango on the street.

examples.hanzi: 我想学一支优美的探戈。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng xué yì zhī yōuměi de tàngē.
examples.english: I want to learn a graceful tango.

components.note: 比 (compare) — two people side by side, one lined up with the other; to compare.
方 (square, direction) — early picture is disputed (a plough-like tool or lashed boats). Sound clue in 房 fáng, 防 fáng, 访 fǎng, 放 fàng.
亠 (lid) — the top. Memory aid: a lid over a bent shape — a square-cornered 'side' or place, as in 地方, 方法.

example.hanzi: 打个比方,大脑就像一台超级计算机。
example.pinyin: Dǎ gè bǐfang, dànǎo jiù xiàng yī tái chāojí jìsuànjī.
example.english: To give an analogy, the brain is like a supercomputer.
example.fact: The human brain runs on roughly 20 watts of power, about what it takes to dimly light a lightbulb, yet performs pattern-recognition tasks that still outpace supercomputers requiring megawatts of electricity for comparable feats.

examples.hanzi: 比方说，我们可以先去买票。
examples.pinyin: Bǐfang shuō, wǒmen kěyǐ xiān qù mǎi piào.
examples.english: For example, we could go buy tickets first.

examples.hanzi: 我们可以拿大海来比方他的胸怀。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen kěyǐ ná dàhǎi lái bǐfang tā de xiōnghuái.
examples.english: We can use the sea as a comparison for his broad mind.

components.note: 大 (big, a person with arms spread) — below carved marks 丰刀: notches cut into tally sticks to record deals, hence contract, as in 契约 and agreement 默契.
纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and binding, as in 红, 给, 经: an agreement binds like a cord.
勺 (sháo) is a loose sound clue for yuē; 勺 also in 药 yào and 钓 diào.

example.hanzi: 双方签订了一份正式契约。
example.pinyin: Shuāngfāng qiāndìngle yī fèn zhèngshì qìyuē.
example.english: Both parties signed a formal contract.
example.fact: Among the oldest known written contracts is a Sumerian clay tablet from around 2100 BCE recording a land sale, inscribed in cuneiform — a reminder that formal written agreements are almost as old as writing itself.

examples.hanzi: 他们签了一份租房契约。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen qiān le yí fèn zūfáng qìyuē.
examples.english: They signed a house rental contract.

examples.hanzi: 这份契约有效期是三年。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fèn qìyuē yǒuxiàoqī shì sān nián.
examples.english: This contract is valid for three years.

components.note: 扌 (hand, 提手旁) — marks hand actions, as in 打 hit, 推 push, 拉 pull; 拐 is turning or making off with, as in 拐弯 turn a corner.

example.hanzi: 你在前面路口向左拐。
example.pinyin: Nǐ zài qiánmiàn lùkǒu xiàng zuǒ guǎi.
example.english: Turn left at the junction ahead.
example.fact: 拐 gives directions: 左拐, 拐弯 (turn a corner). 拐杖 is a walking stick, and 拐骗 is to kidnap or swindle.

examples.hanzi: 到前面的红绿灯往右拐。
examples.pinyin: Dào qiánmiàn de hónglǜdēng wǎng yòu guǎi.
examples.english: Turn right at the traffic light ahead.

examples.hanzi: 不要相信陌生人，免得被拐骗。
examples.pinyin: Bú yào xiāngxìn mòshēngrén, miǎnde bèi guǎipiàn.
examples.english: Don't trust strangers, or you may get tricked.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement, as in 过, 近, 送: to go forward.
井 stands in for 隹 of 進, a loose clue only.
凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.

example.hanzi: 这个仓库每天有大量货物进出。
example.pinyin: Zhège cāngkù měitiān yǒu dàliàng huòwù jìnchū.
example.english: Large quantities of goods move in and out of this warehouse every day.
example.fact: The Port of Shanghai has been the world's busiest container port by volume every year since 2010, handling more than 47 million shipping containers in 2023 alone.

examples.hanzi: 这个小区的进出都要刷卡。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiǎoqū de jìnchū dōu yào shuākǎ.
examples.english: Entering and leaving this residential area both require swiping a card.

examples.hanzi: 大门口有很多人进出。
examples.pinyin: Dà ménkǒu yǒu hěn duō rén jìnchū.
examples.english: Many people go in and out at the main gate.

components.note: 尸 (body, crouching figure) — marks the body and posture, as in 尾 tail, 层, 居 reside; 屈 is bending the body.
月 (moon / flesh) — on the left, likely a squashed 舟 (boat) in 服, not a moon or body part. Dictionary story: a person 卩 putting on a coat 月.
卩 (kneeling person) — on the right, with 又 (hand). The old picture is a hand pressing someone down, 'submit'; clothes (衣服) and service (服务) came later.

example.hanzi: 面对压力,他始终没有屈服。
example.pinyin: Miànduì yālì, tā shǐzhōng méiyǒu qūfú.
example.english: Facing the pressure, he never gave in.
example.fact: During the 872-day Siege of Leningrad in World War II, the city's residents endured extreme famine and cold but never surrendered to the surrounding German forces, one of the longest and most destructive sieges in modern history.

examples.hanzi: 他不愿意向困难屈服。
examples.pinyin: Tā bú yuànyì xiàng kùnnan qūfú.
examples.english: He is unwilling to give in to difficulties.

examples.hanzi: 这个国家最终屈服于外来压力。
examples.pinyin: Zhège guójiā zuìzhōng qūfú yú wàilái yālì.
examples.english: This country finally yielded to outside pressure.
